newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Shipment delay, winter boost Taiwan corn prices.
newsitem.headline: Shipment delay, winter boost Taiwan corn prices.

text.p: Delay for two major corn shipments and increased feed consumption caused by the onset of cooler weather have pushed Taiwan prices for corn and corn products higher in the past week, traders said on Friday.
Average local wholesale corn and corn powder prices were up sharply on Friday from a week earlier, local corn traders said.

Demand for feed products usually peaks in winter due to pigs' better appetites, but traders said delays involving two 54,000-tonne corn shipments also were squeezing local supplies, helping to push prices higher.
Taiwan corn importer Cheng-I Co has acknowledged suffering cash flow problems and bouncing some T$50 million in cheques.

A subsequent cessation of bank credit forced Cheng-I out of the import market and made supplier Peavey Co scramble to resell the two shipments that Cheng-I had bought. Only one of the shipments has found a new buyer, traders said.
Traders said they expect the corn supply gap to be filled within two weeks, allowing local prices to return to normal.

The price of Taiwan wholesale corn powders was T$7.3 to T$7.4 per kg, up from T$6.7-6.8 a week earlier, traders said. Local wholesale corn was T$6.2 to T$6.4 per kg, up from T$5.9 to T$6.0 a week earlier, they said.
